# 1. Exploratory plots

For IBIO830, I need to do some exploratory figures.
Figure1. Distribution of the data:
```{r}
RandomPointsCD_data <- RandomPointsCD_data |>
  mutate(region = ifelse(clan == "serenan" | clan == "serenas" | clan == "happyzebra", "serena", "talek"))
```


```{r}
RandomPointsCD_data$case <- as.factor(RandomPointsCD_data$case)

region_labels <- c("serena" = "Serena", "talek" = "Talek")
loc_labels <- c("0" = "Available Locations", "1" = "Used Locations")


Dist_plots <- ggplot(RandomPointsCD_data) +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = dst_br_, col = case, fill = case), show.legend = F) +
  facet_wrap(~ region + case, ncol = 2, labeller = labeller(region = region_labels, case = loc_labels)) +
  labs(x = "Distance to edge of the territory",
       y = "Counts") +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 15))

Dist_plots
```

The prediction is that hyenas are selecting den locations closer to human communities. Here, human communities will be illustrated as th edge of the territory

For IBIO830: I will use this boxplot, as it looks like it is significant. 
```{r}
boxplot(graph_data_talek$dst_br_ ~ graph_data_talek$case)
```

# 2. Modelling the RSF

ALSO, we need to control for the obs effort (some years field team would go more on obs vs other years/season). I guess with year as a random, and month as a covariable, it does control for this...

------------------------------------------------------------------------
Quick tips for RSF modelling

-   Treat landcover as a categorical predictor (factor) in your logistic/conditional logistic RSF (used vs available).

-   If you used a very fine raster (10 m) but your hyena den location accuracy is coarse (GPS error), consider buffering points or using a majority focal window to reduce misclassification from single-pixel noise.

-   If you want multi-year matching (landcover year of den use), pick the dataset year accordingly (Copernicus 2019 / WorldCover 2020 / MODIS yearly).

## 2.1. RSF model

I will separate the Talek points with the triangle ones, so that I can make a model with the Talek town borders as a variable.

With brms:

```{r brms}

brm_RSF <- brms::brm(case ~ landcover + (1|year) + (1|clan),
                     data = RandomPointsCD_data, 
                     family = bernoulli(),
                     cores = 4, 
                     chains = 4)


```

## 2.2. Distance to Talek model

```{r brms talek model}
CD_RSF_data_tl <- RandomPointsCD_data |>
  filter(clan == "talek")


brm_RSF_tl <- brm(case ~ dst_tl + year + (1|year),
                  data = CD_RSF_data_tl, 
                  family = bernoulli(),
                  cores = 4, 
                  chains = 4)

brm_RSF_tl <- readRDS("brms_models/brm_RSF_tl.rds")

```

```{r}

summary(brm_RSF_tl)
plot(conditional_effects(brm_RSF_tl), points = T)
```
